AGENDA
  YOUTH & FAMILY ACTION COMMITTEE
  Tuesday, September 28, 2021
  6:30 P.M.
  The three-fold mission of the Youth & Family Action Committee is:
  1. To support positive activities and opportunities for young people;
  2. To strengthen families; and
  3. To combat the problems of substance abuse.

Tonight’s meeting will be held virtually in compliance with Governor Newson’s Executive
Order to minimize the spread of the COVID-19 Virus. The meeting will be live streamed on
the La Verne You Tube channel at www.cityoflaverne.org/stream.

To make a comment on an agenda item or under public comment, email your phone
number to cityclerk@cityoflaverne.org. This email address will be monitored live during the
meeting and interested parties will be called. Please be aware there is a delay in the live
stream service and any requests to speak should be submitted as soon as possible.

minutes_text:
LA VERNE YOUTH & FAMILY ACTION COMMITTEE
  Minutes of the Regular Meeting
  September 28, 2021

1. A regular meeting of the Youth & Family Action Committee was called to order by
  Chair Robin Carder at 6:30 p.m.

2. Executive Board Members present (virtually):

  Executive Board
  Robin Carder, Chair - Council Member
  Rick Crosby, Vice Chair - Council Member
  Carolyn Cockrell - Resident
  Denise Fisher - Resident

  Don Kendrick, Resident
  Donna Redman, Resident
  Greg Polatto, Resident/BUSD
  Mark Rodgers, BUSD
  Sam Gonzalez, LVPD
  Janessa Gonzalez, LVPD
  Isela Moreno, Tri-City Mental Health
  Jessica Vozella, American Lung Assoc.
  JR Ranells, City of La Verne
  Alfie Sanchez, Majestic Cycling/Kiwanis International

3. Review of Minutes  Minutes for the June 22, 2021, meeting were
  approved. Don Kendrick followed up on the Teen
  Center grant application but there was not an update
  on its status yet.

4. School Resource Officer  School Resource Officer Janessa Gonzalez provided
  a report to the group. Janessa noted the differences
  in having students fully back on campus this year.
  Janessa shared that vaping is still evident at the high
  school and that there continues to be efforts to
  address this ongoing problem.

  Vice Chair Crosby complimented Janessa on her role
  as the SRO and her ability to engage with the
  students. Chair Carder inquired about Homecoming
  and activities surrounding those festivities.

5. BUSD Report  Mark Rodgers with the Bonita Unified School District
  provided an update regarding the start of the school
  year and continuing impacts of COVID-19. Mark also
  highlighted specific support for students related to
  mental health impacts and learning support.
 Youth & Family Action Committee Minutes September 28, 2021, page 2

  The group also received information on the free
  breakfast and lunch program with an interest in
  YFAC’s support for the Summer Lunch program if
  needed. Lastly, the group had a discussion regarding
  troubling trends related to vandalism promoted on
  social media (TikTok) such as damage to restrooms.
  Janessa shared information on instances that have
  occurred so far and ways to prevent future issues.

  Mark also provided an update on BUSD Member
  changes and the status of designating a YFAC
  representative in October.

6. Ordinance 1100  Jessica Vozella with the American Lung Association
  provided a presentation on the recent adoption by the
  City Council of a Tobacco Ordinance banning all
  flavored tobacco products and the ordinances impacts.
  Jessica shared there is an exception in regard to
  menthol products related to legal challenges as well as
  current La Verne businesses that offer hookah related
  services. Jessica also informed the group that she will
  be wrapping up her work in La Verne at the end of the
  year and thanked the group for all their work toward
  this accomplishment.

  Administrative Lieutenant Sam Gonzalez shared
  information on enforcement related to the ordinance
  and how the Police Department is utilizing its grant
  resources.

  The group thanked Jessica for her many contributions
  to YFAC and the La Verne community.

7. Bicycle Program  Vice Chair Crosby introduced the background for a
  new program distributing bicycles to La Verne youth
  around Christmas time. Rick introduced Alfie Sanchez
  with Majestic Cycling who brought this idea to the City
  and is also a part of La Verne Kiwanis International.
  Alfie shared his vision of distributing 40 free bikes,
  helmets, and locks to the community’s youth around
  Christmas. The specific program details are still being
  ironed out but staff is working directly with Alfie to
  ensure the program can be successful. JR noted that
  staff was looking for general support of this idea and
  that the item would come back in October with more
  specifics.
 Youth & Family Action Committee Minutes September 28, 2021, page 3

8. Youth Representation  JR reported to the group that there is a desire to bring
  back youth representation to YFAC as has been done
  in the past. JR noted how representatives where
  identified in the past and how valuable they were in
  providing insight and perspective with discussion
  issues brought forth to the group. Janessa shared her
  support for a youth representative and will work on
  identifying some students that will be able to
  participate and share their perspective.

9. Public Comment  Greg Palotto noted he is eager to formally be part of
  the group and is learning a great deal.

  Administrative Lieutenant Gonzalez shared information
  regarding the upcoming Public Safety Open House.
  Sam also informed the group of his pending promotion
  to Police Captain and that Lieutenant Chris Dransfeldt
  will be representing the department at future YFAC
  meetings.

  Isela Moreno with Tri-City Mental Health Services
  shared information on the formation of a Transition
  Age Youth Wellness Advisory Council. Isela also
  provided information regarding the upcoming
  stakeholders meeting.

10. Next Meeting  The next YFAC meeting is scheduled for October
  26th at 6:30 p.m.

11. Adjournment  The meeting was adjourned at 7:25 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,

JR Ranells
Assistant to the City Manager
